messages:
Alexa M: Taking the swing starting now (US‑EAST). Quick passoff — can we confirm primary/secondary, PagerDuty escalation rights, Grafana dashboard access, and AWS assume-role perms? I don’t have the temp role in my console yet.

Ben R: I’ll be primary for the first 2 hours. Charlie, can you be secondary from +2h? :thumbsup:

Charlie L: Yep I can take secondary after Ben. I’ll watch the high‑latency alerts.

Alexa M: Thanks. Ben — can you confirm you have the PD escalation policy assigned (SRE‑Prod‑Escalate)? PD sometimes shows limited policies if JIT was used.

Ben R: Confirmed. My PD profile shows SRE‑Prod‑Escalate and I tested an escalation yesterday. pagerduty-bot, can you verify the oncall coverage for this window?

pagerduty-bot: Coverage check: primary=Ben R, secondary=Charlie L, escalation policy=SRE‑Prod‑Escalate. Oncall periods: 2026-03-15T16:00Z → 2026-03-15T18:00Z (primary).

Alexa M: Cool. Grafana — make sure you can see the ops/main dashboard and the alerting folders. Charlie, you probably need ops-read + dashboard link in bookmarks.

Charlie L: Currently I have ops-read but not ops-edit. Can still ack alerts. Link I use: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/main

Alexa M: If anyone lacks Grafana access, file a JIT request but ping me first for emergency bump. Runbook reference: runbook-bot: https://runbooks.redwood/ops/oncall-access (use the assume-role section).

runbook-bot: Runbook snippet: "Assume AWS role: ops.oncall.access". Steps: 1) aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ops.oncall.access --role-session-name OncallSession 2) export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... 3) export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... 4) export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=...

Alexa M: Pasting AWS CLI check — if you see this, your role is fine:
```
aws sts get-caller-identity --query Arn --output text
# expected: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ops.oncall.access/OncallSession
```

Ben R: I ran that and got the expected ARN. One note: our temp creds expire in 1 hour by default; re-run assume-role before expiration or use the console 'extend' flow.

Charlie L: Also, for PagerDuty mobile escalation — make sure your phone contact is verified, PD sometimes drops SMS for new numbers. I tested push notifications earlier.

Alexa M: Important — if an incident is P1, follow escalation: 1) PagerDuty page primary 2) If no ack in 90s, page secondary 3) Call the oncall lead number (Ops Lead) 4) Open bridge and post initial status to #incidents.

Ben R: Noted. I’ll start the initial bridge if we see >50% error spike on the inference cluster. Bridge link template: https://meet.redwood/bridge/{{incident_id}}

oncall-bot: Reminder: Vault JIT tokens active window is 60m. Use `vault login -method=approle` per runbook.

Alexa M: Small access gap to flag — I don’t have Grafana admin to mute noisy alerts (ops-alerts:latency-threshold) — Ben can you mute if we see noisy polymerization?

Ben R: I can mute for short windows. If you need me to do that, @Alexa M call me and I’ll take it.

Charlie L: If we need to grant temporary grafana admin to someone, follow the PAM request process in the runbook. Don’t hand out admin casually.

Alexa M: Agreed. Final checklist: primary=Ben R (2h), secondary=Charlie L, PD escalation policy verified, Grafana access confirmed for both, AWS assume-role confirmed for Ben, Alexa will request JIT for Grafana if needed. If any gaps pop up DM me. :white_check_mark:

Ben R: Logging that I’ve updated the passoff doc: https://docs.redwood/passoffs/3187654321 — added coverage, links, and temp-perm notes.

Charlie L: Got it. I’ll shadow alerts for the first 30m then take over after 2h. Good luck.

Alexa M: Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread pinned to the handoff channel for the shift.

pagerduty-bot: PD notification: acknowledgement received from Ben R at 2026-03-15T16:00:35Z.

oncall-bot: NOTE: If you trigger an automated bridge, include the runbook checklist tag: #ops-bridge-checklist."
